messages:
maria: Opening a follow-up thread for the vendor/dependency outage postmortem. Need a compact action tracker and owners for cloud region, model-registry, and auth-provider mitigations.

dave: Please add owner assignments and realistic deadlines. We should push anything that requires infra changes to next sprint unless it's critical.

leila: From product: customers hit ~40% elevated error rates during the incident window. Main customer pain was Dedicated instances failing requests. We need comms + a mitigation plan.

samir: SRE summary: cascading failure path was: cloud networking flaps -> load shifted to a small set of hosts -> model-registry DB pool exhausted -> external auth calls retried -> auth vendor throttled.

jess: Security note: token introspection failures caused additional latency; we need local validation or caching to survive short vendor blips.

maria: Proposed action items: 
- M1: Cross-region traffic shifting automation + periodic failover drills 	1 owner: dave 	1 due: 2026-04-02 	1 ticket: ENG-3501
- M2: Model-registry fallback to object-store + per-model rate limiter 	1 owner: samir 	1 due: 2026-04-09 	1 ticket: ENG-3510
- M3: Auth provider resilience: local token cache + exponential backoff + vendor escalation 	1 owner: jess 	1 due: 2026-03-31 	1 ticket: SEC-412
- M4: Retry-policy audit across services + safe defaults doc 	1 owner: leila 	1 due: 2026-04-05 	1 ticket: ENG-3522
- M5: Customer comms + SLA impact review for Dedicated 	1 owner: kevin 	1 due: 2026-03-29 	1 ticket: OPS-999

dave: I accept M1. Plan: add env-level health tags and a controller that shifts traffic based on aggregated health signals. Will prototype a manual cutover first.

samir: Accept M2. Implementation notes: snapshot latest model binaries to cold object-store every 10m; serve read-only copies if DB pool > 80% usage for >90s. Also add per-model token buckets.

jess: Accept M3. Filing vendor support case (#AV-7004). Immediate step: short TTL local token cache + jittered backoff. Also will add metrics for failed introspections.

leila: Accept M4. Audit scope: services that call auth provider, retry configs, backoff patterns, and whether retries are bounded. Will deliver a recommended library change if we find common anti-patterns.

kevin: Accept M5. CS will draft proactive template and schedule customer outreach. Ops will review SLA language changes and escalate pricing if needed.

infra-bot: Tickets created: ENG-3501, ENG-3510, ENG-3522. Linked runbook: https://git.redwood/sre/runbooks/vendor-mitigations.md

maria: Prioritization: M3 and M1 are P0 because they reduce blast radius quickly. M2 and M4 are P1. M5 is urgent for customers but can be handled in parallel by CS.

dave: Cost note: cross-region reserved capacity has budget implications. I'll include a cost estimate in ENG-3501 by 2026-03-28 so finance can approve.

samir: Recurring pattern note: our retry behavior during transient upstream errors amplifies vendor throttles. ENG-3522 should include a step to set circuit-breaker defaults and avoid cascading retries.

jess: Also propose we add a "vendor incident" tag to models so model-registry can apply stricter rate limiting automatically during vendor degradation.

maria: Scheduling: follow-up sync Tue 2026-03-30 16:00 UTC. Please post short status updates to this thread as you make progress (PRs, ticket links, vendor case numbers).

pagerbot: Reminder scheduled: follow-up sync on 2026-03-30 16:00:00 UTC.

maria: Thanks everyone. I'll update the formal postmortem with owners, deadlines, and links and mark status "in progress" until all actions are closed.

infra-bot: Current statuses: ENG-3501 open, ENG-3510 open, ENG-3522 open, SEC-412 open.
